plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It tolerates light frosts, so it often keeps flowering in northern temperate gardens when most other plants have finished.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; originated in East Asia, especially China and Japan
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years. In Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and has its own festival, the Festival of Happiness.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular semi-deciduous tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In November the Southern Hemisphere spring is at its peak, and streets and parks turn violet, with fallen blossoms carpeting the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, Argentina and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, thousands of jacarandas bloom in spring. In Australian universities, folklore says that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head before exams, you will pass.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn and early winter, earlier than the common camellia. Its delicate, lightly fragrant flowers open when little else is flowering, and they provide late-season nectar for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Oil pressed from sasanqua seeds is used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: A small woodland tuberous perennial that bears nodding, swept-back pink flowers before or alongside marbled, ivy-shaped leaves. It thrives in dry shade and forms colonies in woodlands and gardens in autumn.
plants.location: Native to southern Europe and western Turkey; naturalized in the UK and gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: After flowering, the seed stalks coil like springs and pull the seed capsules to the ground. Ants then carry the sticky seeds away, spreading the plant.
